subject: Re: DPA & SCCs — evidence checklist and DocuSign orchestration
messages:
From: Anna Kowalska <anna.kowalska@finstone.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finstone.com
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA + SCCs — evidence request and next steps

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Procurement and our legal team are ready to move but they need a short package so our privacy team can sign off. Specifically we need: 

- Executed DPA (we prefer DocuSign) or a plan for execution
- The exact SCC variant you intend to rely on and the redlined IDTA/UK addendum (if applicable)
- Subprocessor inventory and whether any subprocessor processes EU data outside the EEA
- Evidence of transfer risk assessment / adequacy proof for third countries (KMS location, logging retention detail)

Can you send a single packet we can attach to the procurement file by EOD Tuesday? If there are any stickier redlines on the IDTA side we should flag them now.

Appreciate it,
Anna
Anna Kowalska
Head of Procurement, Finstone Bank
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kowalska <anna.kowalska@finstone.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA + SCCs — evidence request and next steps

Hi Anna — thanks, this is very clear. Attaching a starter packet and proposed execution plan. High level: 

1) DPA status: Attached is Redwood_DPA_v3_with_IDTA_redlines.pdf — this includes our proposed UK addendum for customers requiring the IDTA path. We adopted the European Commission standard contractual clauses (SCCs) as the core transfer mechanism; the IDTA addendum bridges UK specifics.

2) Evidence pack: SCCs_adopted_clauses_2027-04-10.docx and subprocessors_inventory_20270410.csv attached. The subprocessors file flags locations and whether data residency applies.

3) Technical proofs: we will provide a short transfer-impact summary and KMS region map. For your immediate review, we confirm master keys are KMS-hosted in eu-west-1 (customer data encryption at rest) and logging retention policy is 90 days by default with enterprise retention options.

4) Execution plan (DocuSign): proposed flow is (a) Finstone counters any IDTA redlines within 3 business days, (b) Redwood legal takes final pass, (c) DocuSign envelope sent with DPA + UK addendum, (d) procurement confirms receipt and retention. We can route signing to a Finstone procurement alias if you prefer.

If your legal wants to propose tracked redlines instead of comments, we can accept those into the attached PDF and mark a DocuSign-ready copy. Let me know if you want a short sync with our legal ops (Ben) today.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales — EMEA
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_with_IDTA_redlines.pdf (pdf), SCCs_adopted_clauses_2027-04-10.docx (docx), subprocessors_inventory_20270410.csv (csv)
From: Anna Kowalska <anna.kowalska@finstone.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finstone.com
Date: 2027-04-11T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA + SCCs — evidence request and next steps

Vanessa — thanks for the quick package. A few clarifications from our privacy team after scanning: 

- The SCCs doc you supplied looks like the Module Two + Module Three mix we're used to, but our counsel wants to confirm the controller-processor clause numbering maps to our preferred UK IDTA addendum language (we will send a redline).
- For subprocessors: please confirm whether any analytics vendors have access to unredacted PII and if any subprocessors are onshore to the US. We need the list flagged for transfers.
- For KMS: can you confirm whether customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) are available for Dedicated accounts; if not, will Redwood provide a signed attestation on key separation?

We will send our redlines by COB tomorrow. Also, we prefer DocuSign if you can create the envelope with signing order set to Finstone first.

Best,
Anna
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: anna.kowalska@finstone.com
Date: 2027-04-12T08:17:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA + SCCs — evidence request and next steps

Team — looping legal/ops commentary inline for Finstone: 

- Subprocessors: analytics vendor (Pulselytics) has access to pseudonymized usage metrics only; no direct access to unredacted PII. We have flagged any subprocessors that process in the US in the CSV.
- BYOK/KMS: customer-managed keys are available for Dedicated and Private customers. For Hosted accounts we offer provider-managed KMS in eu-west-1; we can provide an attestation letter for separation and key rotation practices for procurement.
- SCCs/IDTA: Kar this is a quick ask — can you confirm whether the redline from Finstone requiring a tighter data localization carve-out (Art. 10 style) is a showstopper or we can accept a limited carve with documentation obligations?

I propose we: (a) offer the attestation as an attached PDF, (b) accept limited localization carve (if counsel allows) with an annex describing technical mitigations, (c) prepare the DocuSign envelope and set signing order to Finstone -> Redwood.

I'll build the envelope today assuming no aggressive redlines.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: anna.kowalska@finstone.com
Date: 2027-04-12T17:03:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA + SCCs — evidence request and next steps

Anna / Finstone team — quick read and proposal from our side: 

- Localization carve: we are comfortable accepting a narrowly scoped localization appendix limited to production data for specified regulated workloads. We cannot accept an open-ended localization obligation (operational impracticality). Proposed language: bullet list of impacted data types + obligation to notify Redwood and provide tracking evidence; Redwood will provide an annex of technical mitigations (encryption in transit and at rest, egress controls, logging).
- Attestation: attaching KMS_attestation_20270412.pdf (signed) — confirms provider-managed keys for Hosted and BYOK for Dedicated/Private; includes key separation practices.
- Next steps: If Finstone's redline is transactional (tracked changes) send it back; otherwise we will incorporate the limited localization appendix and send DocuSign envelope by tomorrow morning with signing order Finstone -> Redwood. 

Looking forward to the redlines.
Karthik Iyer
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: KMS_attestation_20270412.pdf (pdf)
